name: Riesenrundgemälde
kurzbeschreibung: The Innsbruck Giant Panoramic Painting at Bergisel captivates visitors with a monumental 360-degree panoramic depiction of the 1809 Tyrolean battles for freedom.
preis: Adults approx. €11.00, concessions €8.50, children free (combined ticket includes Kaiserjägermuseum)
oeffnungszeiten: Year-round Wednesday to Monday 09:00–17:00 (closed on Tuesdays)
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Innsbruck Giant Panoramic Painting (Riesenrundgemälde), housed inside the modern museum Das Tirol Panorama on historic Bergisel hill, is a rare cultural and historical masterpiece of international significance. Covering an immense canvas of approximately 1,000 square meters, the 360-degree cyclorama completed in 1896 dramatically portrays the third Battle of Bergisel fought on August 13, 1809. Under the leadership of folk hero Andreas Hofer, Tyrolean riflemen defended their homeland against combined Bavarian and Napoleonic forces. The circular painting pulls viewers right into the turbulent historical struggle and dramatic alpine landscapes.

Route & Requirements

From a raised central viewing rotunda, visitors experience the astonishing depth of the cyclorama. The seamless combination of two-dimensional oil painting and a sculpted three-dimensional faux terrain—complete with actual rocks, shrubs, dirt mounds, and cannonballs—creates an impeccable optical illusion where picture and physical reality become indistinguishable. The adjoining underground permanent exhibition „Schauplatz Tirol“ utilizes interactive media stations and historical artifacts to explore Tyrolean nature, politics, and cultural identity. The museum is fully accessible with elevators and wide ramps; the visit involves no physical difficulty and is ideal for all ages.

Visit & Arrival

Das Tirol Panorama with the Giant Panoramic Painting is open Wednesday through Monday from 09:00 to 17:00 (closed on Tuesdays). General admission for adults is approx. €11.00 and includes admission to the neighboring Kaiserjägermuseum; admission is free for children and youths up to 19 years of age. Admission is free with the Innsbruck Card. Public transit: tram line 1 and the Sightseer bus stop directly at Bergisel. By car, leave the Brenner Autobahn A13 at the Innsbruck Süd exit and follow clear signage to the pay-and-display parking lots on the Bergisel plateau.

Tips

Combine your museum tour with a scenic stroll along the Bergisel Panorama Trail, providing dramatic vistas down into the rugged Sill Gorge and across Innsbruck. Just steps away stands the world-renowned Bergisel Ski Jump designed by star architect Zaha Hadid; its tower restaurant offers a spectacular 360-degree alpine panorama of the Nordkette mountains. The nearby Andreas Hofer monument in the park is also worth viewing.
